messages.subject: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.subject_clean: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I’m  trying to fit an exponential east-west density model with secr. I have read the pdf on modelling density surfaces and understand that I need to provide a user defined function for the density surface via the details=list(UserDfn) component.  It seems fairly straight forward but I’m getting an error to do with the start values.

I’ve written a function (based on the example in the pdf) as follows:

ExpDens <- function (Dbeta=c(-0.4,0.0025), mask_=mask, ngroups=1, nsessions= 1) {

  if (Dbeta[1] == 'name') return ('0')

  if (Dbeta[1] == 'parameters') return ('intercept')

  D <- exp(Dbeta[1]+Dbeta[2]*covariates(mask_)$X.coord) ## east-west exponential

  tempD <- array(D, dim = c(nrow(mask_), 1, 1))

  return(tempD)

}

But when I try use this function with secr.fit in the following way:

mod <- secr.fit (CH.multi, details = list(userDfn = ExpDens), start=c(int1, slope1, logit(0.2), log(100)), mask, detectfn = 0, trace = FALSE, verify = FALSE, buffer= 400)

I get the following error: Error: length(start) == NP is not TRUE.
The pdf says that one needs to provide starting values via the start argument but I'm obviously doing something wrong.

A second issue I had was with providing arguments to the function. This is why in the function above I set the defaults to be the values I need. So initially the function arguments did not have defaults and my call to secr.fit looked as follows:

mod <- secr.fit (CH.multi, details = list(userDfn = ExpDens(Dbeta=c(int1,slope1), mask, 1,1)), start=c(int1, slope1, logit(0.2), log(100)), mask, detectfn = 0, buffer= 400)

and I got this error:

Error in secr.fit(CH.multi, details = list(userDfn = ExpDens(Dbeta = c(int1,  :

  details$userDfn should be a function

I suspect I am doing something small syntactically wrong, any ideas?
Thanks a lot!

Greg

messages.subject: Re: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.subject_clean: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.body_plain:
You don’t need to use a user-defined function for this. Just use D~x in the formula for D. The default link function is the log link so this gives you exponential trend in density as a function of x. See page 3 of the secr densitysurfaces vignette.

messages.subject: secr 2.9.0
messages.body_plain:
secr 2.9.0, now on CRAN <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/secr>, is the first major release for several months. The vignettes have been updated (they now use RMarkdown, RStudio and knitr) and a new dataset has been added (OVpossum). The 'fxi' functions have been extended (but do read the vignette secr-densitysurfaces.pdf <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-densitysurfaces.pdf>!). Users may provide their own non-Euclidean distance matrix or function. Regression spline smooths are enabled (using mgcv to construct the basis functions, as proposed by Borchers and Kidney in prep.).  Plotting of density surfaces has been improved, and a legend is added by default. Function secr.test() is provided for Monte Carlo goodness-of-fit testing. Several interface bugs are fixed - my thanks to people who have reported them.

See also the secr page <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html> on the Density website.

Murray

messages.body_plain:
I see that secr 2.9.0 fails checks for r-release-osx-x86_64-mavericks <http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html#r-release-osx-x86_64-mavericks> because other packages are not available to run the examples (‘spsurvey’ and ‘rgeos’, but specifically ‘rgdal'). Murray

messages.subject: Re: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.subject_clean: Using a user defined function to model a density surface
messages.body_plain:
Hi again
Sorry it took a while to get back to this... I think you had a couple of minor errors (need to specify 2 parameter names, and I've forgotten the other one; specifying default values for Dbeta is pointless  - they're never used). Here I compare the 'D~x' solution and a minimally modified version of your code. Seems OK (I had some scary moments when I thought the just-released version might break it)
Murray

ExpDens <- function (Dbeta, mask_=mask, ngroups=1, nsessions= 1) {

  if (Dbeta[1] == 'name') return ('0')

  if (Dbeta[1] == 'parameters') return (c('intercept','slope'))

  ## standardise so comparable with D~x
  mx <- mean(mask_$x)
  sdx <- sd(mask_$x)
  stdx <- (mask_$x - mx) / sdx

  D <- exp(Dbeta[1] + Dbeta[2] * stdx) ## east-west exponential

  tempD <- array(D, dim = c(nrow(mask_), 1, 1))

  return(tempD)

}

mask <- make.mask(traps(captdata))

## doing it the hard way
mod <- secr.fit (captdata, details = list(userDfn = ExpDens),
     start=c(2, 0, logit(0.2), log(25)), mask = mask, detectfn = 0,
     trace = FALSE, verify = FALSE)

## the conventional method for east-west exponential gradient
modx <- secr.fit (captdata, model = D~x, start=c(2, 0, logit(0.2), log(25)),
    mask = mask, detectfn = 0, trace = FALSE, verify = FALSE)

> coef(mod)
beta    SE.beta        lcl        ucl
D.intercept  1.70082187 0.11763853  1.4702546  1.9313892
D.slope      0.01295184 0.14676598 -0.2747042  0.3006079
g0          -0.97863904 0.13625085 -1.2456858 -0.7115923
sigma        3.37997729 0.04444784  3.2928611  3.4670935

> coef(modx)
beta    SE.beta        lcl        ucl
D      1.70082187 0.11763853  1.4702546  1.9313892
D.x    0.01295184 0.14676598 -0.2747042  0.3006079
g0    -0.97863904 0.13625085 -1.2456858 -0.7115923
sigma  3.37997729 0.04444784  3.2928611  3.4670935
